title: Delete Columns to Make Sorted
summary: Given an array of n strings of equal length, arrange the strings in a grid format.
statement: Given an array of n strings of equal length, arrange the strings in a grid format. Identify and delete any columns that are not sorted lexicographically. Return the count of such columns that are deleted.
constraints: Delete each column whose top-to-bottom characters are not nondecreasing; return the count.
reference_solution:
def unsorted_column_count(strs):
 return sum(any(a>b for a,b in zip(column,column[1:])) for column in zip(*strs))
hints: Columns are independent in this version.
Transpose conceptually and inspect adjacent characters in each column.
Count a column if any upper character is greater than the next lower one.
Adjacent nondecrease is necessary and sufficient for a fully sorted column.
editorial: Adjacent nondecrease is necessary and sufficient for a fully sorted column.

tests.explanation: Only the second column b,a,h decreases, so one column is deleted.
The single column is already sorted.
